newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money eases slightly but remains high.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money eases slightly but remains high.

text.p: Dutch call money retreated from the peaks it had reached in Wednesday's session, the day before Thursday's Ascension Day holiday, but remained at high levels on Friday.
Overnight money had changed hands up to 3.50 percent on Wednesday, when liquidity seemed to be unevenly divided between money market participants, dealers said.

They had expected overnight rates to ease toward 3.06 percent with the allocation of a new special advances pact on Friday morning, but call continued to trade at a fairly high level, changing hands between 3.25 and 3.31 percent.
"It didn't get further out of control," one dealer said.
He considered this morning's allocation under the new special advances pact reasonable, and said he expected call money to ease further next week to some 3.13 or 3.25 percent.

The Dutch central bank allocated 3.31 billion guilders to the money market this morning, under a new seven-day special advances pact. The pact replaced a 2.83 billion guilder pact of the same duration.
One trader said money seemed to be still unevenly divided between market players and added he not expect call rates to come down significantly before May 23.
"The unusually short (quota scheme) has confused the market a bit. People don't know how to react upon it exactly so they take they sure for the unsure," he said.
The current quota-scheme under which banks borrow from the central bank at the secured loans rate runs from April 18 until May 23, far shorter than the usual 90 days.

Dutch Treasury Certificates maturing in June were priced at 3.13 percent by the Finance Ministry's Agency, one basis point higher than on Wednesday, but dealers said primary trade in them was close to nil.
"Nobody takes that serious, I don't think anything has been done," one dealer said.
Except for call, money market rates were broadly unchanged.
Dealers said trade was quiet many parties had fixed their money earlier this week and had taken a long weekend.
The guilder was virtually unchanged against the mark, trading at 1.12465 per 100 marks.
